threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, roles, and timeline for the budgeting process rollout.

messages.text:
Kicking off the rollout of our standardized budgeting and forecasting process for the next planning cycle.

Scope I am proposing for this first cycle:
- Document the end-to-end budgeting and forecasting process in a single place (linked to the future process doc A3)
- Map current practices and pain points across departments so we know what we are changing (T1)
- Define the governance and approval workflow for budgets (T6)
- Deliver standard templates and a 12‑month rolling forecast model in parallel threads

Roles for this thread:
- 440036 to coordinate T1 and keep us honest on timelines and documentation
- 98074 and 44926 to support with current templates, cut-offs, and any constraints from the accounting side
- I will consolidate the overall plan and align with the finance director.

Can you confirm responsibilities and flag anything missing from the scope before we lock it in for this first rollout?

Confirmed from my side. I can take the lead on T1 and also start sketching the structure for the process description so that A3 does not become a last‑minute exercise.

For scope, I would explicitly call out:
- Training and handover as part of the first cycle, even if materials are light at first
- A clear link between the approval workflow in T6 and the reporting cadence, so managers know when they will see budget vs actuals.

If everyone agrees, I will draft a simple RACI for T1 and T6 and share it here by tomorrow.

From accounting side, I can support with current templates and timelines.

For T1, I can provide:
- Copies of the existing budget spreadsheets and any ad‑hoc forecast files we used last year
- A quick list of our current submission deadlines and who usually sends what.

On T6, I will need guidance from you on the approval steps, but I can describe how we currently sign off budgets informally so we have a starting point.

I can help by pulling the current bookkeeping exports we use for budget support and cash‑flow checks.

For T1, I will:
- List the files and reports departments usually ask for when preparing their numbers
- Note any recurring issues I see when they request data, like missing cost centers or unclear account groupings.

Let me know if you want me to already tag which ledgers are more relevant for the new process, or if that comes later with the forecast work.

Thanks all. From my side, I will:
- Support 411661 on aligning the overall plan with the finance director
- Help define the governance in T6, especially around escalation and cut‑off dates.

One question on scope: do we want the first cycle to already include a full 12‑month rolling forecast, or do we start with the annual budget plus a simpler cash‑flow view and then extend it? This will impact how we describe the process in A3.

Good point. Given the 21‑day window and the need to avoid disrupting month‑end, I suggest we keep the first cycle focused on:
- Standardized annual budget template
- 12‑month rolling cash‑flow forecast at a higher level of detail, not line‑by‑line.

We can document in A3 that the forecast granularity will be refined after the pilot.

If no one objects, I would like to lock this as the scope for the first rollout cycle so we can move on to the timeline.

No objection from me. I will reflect that in the draft outline for A3: first cycle with annual budget plus higher‑level 12‑month cash‑flow, with a note that we revisit detail after the pilot.

On responsibilities, I will also include a simple table mapping T1 and T6 owners and contributors so we have a clear reference.

Works for me. A higher‑level 12‑month view is more realistic for now.

For the timeline, we should avoid heavy workshops during the first five business days of the month because of closing. Maybe we can cluster T1 interviews and the first draft of the governance (T6) in the middle of the month.

Agreed on avoiding close. Here is a strawman timeline leading to go‑live aligned with the next fiscal quarter planning:
- Days 1‑5: Collect existing templates and current practices (input to T1)
- Days 6‑10: Run short interviews / surveys and draft the process outline for A3
- Days 11‑15: Draft governance and approval workflow (T6) and validate with finance leadership
- Days 16‑21: Finalize scope doc A3 for this cycle and hand over to the template and pilot threads.

If we align on this, we can treat it as our baseline plan and adjust only if we hit major blockers.

The timeline works for me. I will share it with the finance director and confirm there are no conflicts with other initiatives.

One small suggestion: for T1, we might want to prioritize departments with larger budgets in the first few days so their input shapes the process early.

I will take the timeline you proposed and translate it into a simple checklist for T1 and T6 with owners and due dates.

I will also draft a short summary paragraph for A3 describing this first‑cycle scope and timing so we have a consistent message for stakeholders.

On my side, I will need a bit more time around month‑end to pull data, but the proposed dates are fine.

I will start gathering the reports for T1 this week so we are not rushed later.

Thanks all. To close this thread:
- Scope for the first rollout cycle is confirmed: standardized annual budget template plus higher‑level 12‑month cash‑flow, documented in A3
- Overall timeline and milestones are agreed as per M9, with T1 and T6 as the main focus here.

Next steps are below; we will track progress in the upcoming check‑ins.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the standard budget and cash-flow templates.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the standard budget template based on our current files and the chart of accounts.

Key points in A1 draft:
- Separate tabs for income, operating expenses, and a simple balance‑sheet view
- Columns for monthly figures plus a total column for the year
- Basic mapping to our main account groups so we can reconcile with actuals later (T2).

For the cash‑flow side, I used the structure from the rolling model A2 as a starting point, but it is still rough. I would appreciate feedback on:
- Level of detail per cost category
- Whether we should include headcount lines in this first version.

Please share comments so we can converge on the structure and assumptions.

Thanks for the draft. From a process perspective, I would suggest we keep the template as lean as possible for the first cycle.

On A1:
- Income: group by main revenue streams, not by individual customer
- Opex: group by nature (personnel, rent, marketing, etc.) with a free‑text field for explanations
- Balance‑sheet: only the key items that drive cash (receivables, payables, inventory).

For A2, I would like to align on a small set of cash‑in and cash‑out categories and a few standard assumptions, then we can refine later. We can use A7 to document those assumptions.

Let us first agree on the structure of A1 before we lock it in.

I went through the draft A1 and have a few usability comments:
- Could we freeze the header row and the department column so managers do not lose context when scrolling?
- It might help to add a short instruction tab that we can later reuse in the user guide A6.

On level of detail, I agree with 411661: keep it grouped by main categories for now. We can always add more lines after the pilot if needed.

For T2, I suggest we explicitly list which chart‑of‑account ranges map to each section so reconciliation is straightforward.

From a forecasting angle, I would keep headcount in a separate, simple section in A1: number of FTEs and total personnel cost per month. That should be enough for now.

For A2 and A7, I propose we start with these cash‑flow categories:
- Cash‑in: customer receipts, other income
- Cash‑out: payroll, suppliers, rent and utilities, taxes, debt service, other.

Assumptions to capture in A7:
- Average collection period for customers
- Average payment terms for suppliers
- Timing of tax and loan payments.

If this sounds reasonable, we can refine the exact wording and then test the model with recent data as part of T3.

Understood. I will:
- Adjust A1 so that income and opex are grouped as suggested
- Add a simple headcount and total personnel cost section
- Add an instructions tab that we can later align with A6.

For A2, I will rework the categories to match the list you proposed and start drafting the assumptions in A7. I will need help validating the collection and payment terms, since I only have a partial view from the accounting side.

I can help by checking recent bookkeeping data to see the usual timing for customer receipts and supplier payments.

I will pull a quick sample from the last few months so we have a rough idea for A7. It might not be perfect, but it should give us a starting point for T3 testing.

The proposed categories and assumptions look workable for the first cycle.

Before we formally approve A1, can we confirm:
- That every line in the template can be mapped to an account group for reconciliation (T2)
- That the headcount section is clearly separated so HR‑related data is easy to maintain.

Once 98074 updates the draft, I suggest we treat that structure as final for this cycle, with only minor tweaks allowed after the pilot.

I have updated A1 accordingly:
- All lines now have a corresponding account group code in a hidden mapping column
- Headcount and personnel cost are in a separate section at the bottom of the income tab.

From my side, the structure is stable enough for this first cycle. If you agree, we can mark the layout as approved and move on to fine‑tuning A2 and A7.

Confirmed from my side: the structure of A1 works for the planning discussions we need to have.

On A2 and A7, I suggest we lock in the initial assumptions as:
- Customer receipts: average 45 days after invoice
- Supplier payments: average 30 days after invoice
- Taxes: monthly, paid in the following month
- Debt service: as per current loan schedules.

We can test these in T3 using the last six months of data and adjust if the gaps are too large.

Great. To summarize this thread:
- The structure and level of detail of the standard budget template A1 are approved for the first cycle
- Initial cash‑flow categories and key assumptions for A2 are agreed and will be documented in A7, then tested in T3.

We will revisit both after the pilot, but for now we can proceed with these as our baseline.

threads.thread_goal: Resolve data quality issues and confirm the baseline dataset.

messages.text:
I have started the reconciliation work for T4 and wanted to share initial findings.

So far I checked the main ledgers for the last 12 months:
- Bank and cash: mostly reconciled, a few small timing differences
- Receivables: some old open items that may not be collectible
- Payables: a few invoices booked late compared to the service period.

These issues could affect the baseline we use for the budget vs actual template A5 and the cash‑flow model. I am not fully sure which periods and ledgers we should prioritize as the official baseline.

Looking for guidance on how strict we need to be for this first cycle.

Thanks for the summary. For T4, I would focus on getting the last 12 months of P and L and key balance‑sheet items consistent enough to feed A5 and the forecast model.

My suggestion:
- Prioritize reconciliation of bank, receivables, and payables for the last 12 months
- Flag any doubtful receivables separately so we can decide how to treat them in the forecast.

We do not need perfection for older periods, but the last year should be as clean as we can make it within the timeline.

From a planning perspective, we mainly need a reliable baseline for the last 12 months to feed into A5 and the rolling forecast.

I propose we define the baseline as:
- Period: last 12 closed months
- Ledgers: bank, receivables, payables, and main revenue and expense accounts.

For doubtful receivables, let us keep them in a separate list so we can decide whether to exclude them from the cash‑flow assumptions later.

I agree with that approach. For the forecast testing, we will mainly use:
- Monthly revenue and expense totals
- Movements in receivables and payables
- Bank balances.

As long as those are reconciled for the last 12 months, we can work with some imperfections elsewhere. We just need to be transparent about any limitations when we present the first A5 reports.

Understood. I will:
- Focus on reconciling bank, receivables, and payables for the last 12 months
- Create a separate list of doubtful receivables and late‑booked invoices.

Once that is done, I will export the baseline dataset and share the location so it can be used for A5 and the forecast tests.

When you export the baseline, please include:
- Monthly trial balance for the last 12 months
- Separate tabs for receivables and payables aging.

That will make it easier for me to build the first pilot of A5 and check that the variances line up with the accounting records.

I can do that. It might take me a bit longer to prepare the aging reports, but I will aim to have the full export ready by the end of the week.

If I run into any issues with the older items, I will flag them separately instead of delaying the whole dataset.

Given the time constraints, I suggest we formally define the baseline as:
- Period: last 12 closed months
- Ledgers: bank, receivables, payables, and main revenue and expense accounts, reconciled as per T4.

Any items older than that or not reconciled in time will be documented as limitations but not block the rollout.

If there are no objections, we can record this as our baseline definition for the first cycle.

No objection from me. Once the baseline export is ready, I will use it together with 98074 to test the forecast model and the first A5 report.

We will note any data quality caveats when we present the results to stakeholders.

Agreed. Once 44926 shares the export, I will:
- Build a first draft of A5 using one recent month
- Check that totals match the trial balance and highlight any gaps.

This will also help us confirm that the baseline is usable for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and execute the pilot with one business unit and capture feedback.

messages.text:
With the templates and baseline coming together, we should plan the pilot for the new process.

Proposal:
- Pilot unit: the business unit with the largest volume of transactions, so we stress‑test A1, A2, and A5 properly
- Timing: start collecting their budget using A1 next week, then build a 12‑month cash‑flow using A2 as part of T9.

During the pilot, we will log all issues and suggestions in A8 so we can decide what to adjust before full rollout.

Thoughts on which unit to pick and whether the timing works?

I support piloting with a larger unit, but we need to be careful with their workload.

I suggest we choose the unit that already has a relatively structured budgeting practice, even if it is not the absolute largest. That way, we can focus feedback on the new templates and process rather than basic budgeting concepts.

On timing, next week works as long as we avoid their local month‑end activities.

From a coordination standpoint, I would recommend:
- Selecting the unit that has a manager who is responsive and open to testing new tools
- Scheduling a short kickoff call to walk them through A1 and the basic cash‑flow view from A2.

I can help prepare a simple one‑pager and a short script for that session and set up A8 to capture feedback in a structured way (e.g., template issues, process issues, data issues).

Whichever unit we choose, I can support by:
- Pre‑filling A1 with their last year actuals where possible
- Being on call for questions about account groupings and how to map their costs.

I would prefer a unit that already sends us relatively clean data, so we do not spend the pilot fixing basic coding issues.

From what I see in the bookkeeping, Unit A usually has more consistent postings and fewer late invoices than some others.

If we go with them, I can quickly check that their recent data lines up with the baseline we are using for A5 so we do not confuse them with mismatched numbers.

Based on that, I propose we select Unit A as the pilot business unit.

Tentative schedule for T9:
- Week 1: Kickoff with Unit A, explain A1 and the high‑level cash‑flow view from A2
- Week 2: Unit A completes their budget in A1 and we build their 12‑month cash‑flow
- Week 3: Review results with them, capture feedback in A8, and agree on improvement actions.

If there are no strong objections, I would like to confirm this plan so we can start scheduling.

No objection from me. Unit A is a good choice given their existing discipline.

During the pilot, let us pay special attention to:
- Whether A1 is clear enough without extra explanations
- How much manual work is needed to produce A5 for them
- Whether the cash‑flow assumptions in A2 feel realistic from their perspective.

We should capture all of this in A8 so we have a solid basis for adjustments.

I will reach out to Unit A today to:
- Confirm their availability for the pilot window
- Schedule the kickoff session
- Share a short overview of what we expect from them.

I will also set up A8 with simple fields: issue type, description, impact, and suggested fix. That should make it easier to review and prioritize changes later.

Once Unit A sends back their completed A1, I will:
- Check for any recurring confusion on account groupings
- Build a first A5 report for them so they can see how their budget will be monitored.

Any issues they raise with the layout or mapping I will log directly into A8.

During the review meeting with Unit A, I will focus on:
- Whether the approval steps feel clear and manageable
- How comfortable they are with the cash‑flow assumptions in A2
- Any suggestions they have to simplify the process.

Based on what we capture in A8, we will need to decide which changes to implement before full rollout and which to park for later.

Once we have the feedback logged in A8, I suggest we categorize potential changes into:
- Must‑do before full rollout (e.g., confusing fields in A1, blocking issues in A2 or A5)
- Nice‑to‑have for later cycles.

We should then agree on a small set of concrete adjustments for this first go‑live so we do not overcomplicate the process.

Agreed. For this first rollout, I propose we commit to implementing only the following types of changes based on the pilot:
- Clarifications in labels and instructions in A1
- Minor structural tweaks in A2 that do not break the agreed categories
- Small layout improvements in A5 to make variances easier to read.

More substantial redesigns can be scheduled for a later cycle once we have more experience.

If everyone is aligned, we can record this as our approach to handling pilot feedback.

That works for me. We will treat the pilot as a way to fine‑tune usability and clarity, not to reopen the entire design.

To close this thread:
- Pilot unit confirmed as Unit A, with the three‑week schedule outlined in M39
- Approach to changes based on A8 feedback agreed as per M45.

We will track T9 progress in our regular check‑ins.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize controls, documentation, and training before full rollout.

messages.text:
With the pilot plan in motion, I have drafted the main process and training materials for the rollout.

Highlights:
- A3: end‑to‑end budgeting and forecasting process description, including roles, timelines, and links to A1, A2, A5, and A8
- A6: user guide for the budget template and deadlines, aligned with what we tested in the pilot
- Draft internal control checklist A4, based on the work in T7, covering data entry, review, and sign‑off steps.

I would like your review on:
- Whether the controls in A4 are sufficient and realistic
- Any gaps in the process description A3
- Whether A6 is clear enough for managers who are less familiar with finance.

Once we are comfortable, we can move to formal sign‑off for go‑live.

I reviewed A4 and have a few comments:
- For data entry controls, we might add a simple check that totals in A1 match the system exports before submission
- For review controls, we should specify who checks tax‑sensitive lines, even if the detailed tax review is part of T11.

Overall, the checklist looks manageable. I will also cross‑check A3 and A6 against our statutory reporting requirements as part of T11 and flag any issues.

On A3, I like the overall flow. A couple of suggestions:
- Make the link between the governance workflow (T6) and the internal controls in A4 more explicit, so people see how approvals and checks fit together
- Add a short section on how we will use A5 and the quarterly reviews from T12 to refine assumptions over time.

For A6, I would keep the language as simple as possible and avoid technical terms where we can.

From a governance and risk angle, I would like to see in A4:
- A clear step where someone checks that the cash‑flow assumptions in A2 and A7 are still valid at least quarterly (linked to T12)
- A simple sign‑off record for each cycle, even if it is just a short note in the channel.

On A3, it would help to include a short escalation path if deadlines are missed, given the tight planning window.

I went through A6 from the perspective of someone who is not in finance every day. It is mostly clear.

One suggestion: maybe add a small example showing how a typical expense should be entered in A1, including which account group to choose. That might reduce basic questions later.

Thanks for the feedback. I will:
- Add the total‑check step between A1 and the system exports into A4
- Clarify in A4 who reviews tax‑sensitive lines, and reference T11 for the deeper compliance review
- Update A3 to show how T6 approvals and A4 controls connect.

I will also add a simple example to A6 as suggested.

I will incorporate your points into T11 and T7:
- In A4, I will add a control that confirms the quarterly review of assumptions in A2 and A7 has been performed, linked to T12
- In T11, I will document that we checked tax‑related assumptions and statutory reporting requirements and record a short sign‑off note in the channel.

Once I finish the compliance check, I will confirm that A3, A4, and A6 are aligned with our obligations.

Once T11 is complete, I would like a short summary here confirming:
- Key tax‑related assumptions reviewed
- Any limitations we should be aware of for this first cycle
- Confirmation that the internal control checklist A4 covers the main compliance points.

With that, I will be comfortable recommending sign‑off to the finance director.

I have completed the T11 review:
- Tax‑related assumptions in A2 and A7 are consistent with current legislation
- Statutory reporting requirements are reflected in how we structure A5 and the underlying accounts
- A4 includes checks for tax‑sensitive lines and a quarterly confirmation step.

There are a few minor limitations (e.g., some edge cases for specific deductions), but they do not affect the main budgeting and forecasting process. From my side, A3, A4, and A6 are acceptable for go‑live.

Thanks for closing out T11.

On T12, I propose we set the quarterly review cadence as follows:
- Review of forecast assumptions and performance in the second month of each quarter
- Participants: finance managers, accountant, and a representative from one or two business units
- Inputs: latest A5 reports, updated A2 and A7 assumptions, and any issues logged since the last review.

If we agree on this, we can finalize T12 and include the schedule in A3.

The proposed cadence and participants for T12 work for me. I will add the recurring meetings to the calendar once we confirm the exact dates.

With T11 and T12 defined, and the updates to A3, A4, and A6 in place, I believe we are ready to sign off on controls, documentation, and training for this first rollout.

Agreed. From my side:
- A3 reflects the agreed process, roles, and timelines
- A4 contains practical controls that teams can actually perform
- A6 and the training materials from T8 are ready to be shared with managers.

I suggest we record that we have signed off on these items for go‑live and move to communication and scheduling of the first full cycle.

To close this out:
- Internal controls (A4), process documentation (A3), and training plan and materials (A6, T8) are approved for the first rollout cycle
- Compliance review under T11 is complete, and the quarterly review cadence under T12 is defined.

We can now proceed to communicate the new process and start the first full budgeting and forecasting cycle using the standardized approach.
